# BAES Author — Publication and Research Profile v0.1

**Author:** Babak Rasti M. (بابک راستی میمندی)

## Profile

Babak Rasti M. is a Software Engineer, Systems Architect, and Independent Researcher in Human–AI Engineering, with 28 years of hands-on experience in software engineering and architecture.

His current principal research and engineering project is BAES (Babak AI Engineering Standard), a technology-neutral engineering standard under development for Human–AI Engineering.

His research interests include:

- Human–AI interaction and engineering boundaries
- Human intent, authority, delegation, and authorized execution
- AI reasoning, evidence, challenge, recommendation, and decision boundaries
- Agentic and autonomous AI systems
- Traceability and accountability in AI-intensive systems
- Engineering treatment of long-lived and complex socio-technical systems
- Relationship and potential overlap between emerging Human–AI engineering concerns and existing research, standards, governance, assurance, and systems-engineering practices

## Research Position

BAES is presented as a work in development, not as an independently validated academic result.

The research posture is explicitly open to:

- prior-art and literature identification;
- conceptual criticism;
- counterexamples and boundary cases;
- comparison with existing frameworks and standards;
- empirical or engineering evaluation;
- analysis of redundancy or unnecessary distinctions;
- identification of contexts where the proposed formulation provides little or no value;
- evidence that should lead to revision, limitation, or rejection.

The author does not use biography, experience, or authorship as a substitute for evidence supporting BAES claims.

## Interdisciplinary Interests

Babak also works on independent technical and linguistic projects, including AI-assisted study of Old Persian / Achaemenid cuneiform. Such projects may be presented separately when relevant to an academic audience.

## Public Status

BAES is under development and being prepared for critical external technical and research review. No claim is made here of universal applicability, formal standards recognition, demonstrated superiority, or independent external validation.
